    52	# PPTX Manipulation Skill
    53	
    54	## Overview
    55	
    56	This skill enables programmatic creation, editing, and manipulation of Microsoft PowerPoint (.pptx) presentations using the **python-pptx** library. Create professional slides with text, shapes, images, charts, and tables without manual editing.
    57	
    58	## How to Use
    59	
    60	1. Describe the presentation you want to create or modify
    61	2. Provide content, data, or images to include
    62	3. I'll generate python-pptx code and execute it
    63	
    64	**Example prompts:**
    65	- "Create a 10-slide pitch deck from this outline"
    66	- "Add a chart to slide 3 with this data"
    67	- "Extract all text from this presentation"
    68	- "Generate slides from this markdown content"
    69	
    70	## Domain Knowledge
    71	
    72	### python-pptx Fundamentals
    73	
    74	```python
    75	from pptx import Presentation
    76	from pptx.util import Inches, Pt
    77	from pptx.enum.shapes import MSO_SHAPE
    78	from pptx.enum.text import PP_ALIGN
    79	
    80	# Create new presentation
    81	prs = Presentation()
    82	
    83	# Or open existing
    84	prs = Presentation('existing.pptx')
    85	```
    86	
    87	### Presentation Structure
    88	```
    89	Presentation
    90	├── slide_layouts (predefined layouts)
    91	├── slides (individual slides)
    92	│   ├── shapes (text, images, charts)
    93	│   │   ├── text_frame (paragraphs)
    94	│   │   └── table (rows, cells)
    95	│   └── placeholders (title, content)
    96	└── slide_masters (templates)
    97	```
    98	
    99	### Slide Layouts
   100	```python
   101	# Common layout indices (may vary by template)
   102	TITLE_SLIDE = 0
   103	TITLE_CONTENT = 1
   104	SECTION_HEADER = 2
   105	TWO_CONTENT = 3
   106	COMPARISON = 4
   107	TITLE_ONLY = 5
   108	BLANK = 6
   109	
   110	# Add slide with layout
   111	slide_layout = prs.slide_layouts[TITLE_CONTENT]
   112	slide = prs.slides.add_slide(slide_layout)
   113	```
   114	
   115	### Adding Content
   116	
   117	#### Title Slide
   118	```python
   119	slide_layout = prs.slide_layouts[0]  # Title slide
   120	slide = prs.slides.add_slide(slide_layout)
   121	
   122	title = slide.shapes.title
   123	subtitle = slide.placeholders[1]
   124	
   125	title.text = "Quarterly Report"
   126	subtitle.text = "Q4 2024 Performance Review"
   127	```
   128	
   129	#### Text Content
   130	```python
   131	# Using placeholder
   132	body = slide.placeholders[1]
   133	tf = body.text_frame
   134	tf.text = "First bullet point"
   135	
   136	# Add more paragraphs
   137	p = tf.add_paragraph()
   138	p.text = "Second bullet point"
   139	p.level = 0
   140	
   141	p = tf.add_paragraph()
   142	p.text = "Sub-bullet"
   143	p.level = 1
   144	```
   145	
   146	#### Text Box
   147	```python
   148	from pptx.util import Inches, Pt
   149	
   150	left = Inches(1)
   151	top = Inches(2)
   152	width = Inches(4)
   153	height = Inches(1)
   154	
   155	txBox = slide.shapes.add_textbox(left, top, width, height)
   156	tf = txBox.text_frame
   157	
   158	p = tf.paragraphs[0]
   159	p.text = "Custom text box"
   160	p.font.bold = True
   161	p.font.size = Pt(18)
   162	```
   163	
   164	#### Shapes
   165	```python
   166	from pptx.enum.shapes import MSO_SHAPE
   167	
   168	# Rectangle
   169	shape = slide.shapes.add_shape(
   170	    MSO_SHAPE.RECTANGLE,
   171	    Inches(1), Inches(2),  # left, top
   172	    Inches(3), Inches(1.5) # width, height
   173	)
   174	shape.text = "Rectangle with text"
   175	
   176	# Common shapes:
   177	# MSO_SHAPE.RECTANGLE, ROUNDED_RECTANGLE
   178	# MSO_SHAPE.OVAL, CHEVRON, ARROW_RIGHT
   179	# MSO_SHAPE.CALLOUT_ROUNDED_RECTANGLE
   180	```
   181	
   182	#### Images
   183	```python
   184	# Add image
   185	slide.shapes.add_picture(
   186	    'image.png',
   187	    Inches(1), Inches(2),  # position
   188	    width=Inches(4)        # auto height
   189	)
   190	
   191	# Or specify both dimensions
   192	slide.shapes.add_picture(
   193	    'logo.png',
   194	    Inches(8), Inches(0.5),
   195	    Inches(1.5), Inches(0.75)
   196	)
   197	```
   198	
   199	### Tables
   200	```python
   201	# Create table
   202	rows, cols = 4, 3
   203	left = Inches(1)
   204	top = Inches(2)
   205	width = Inches(8)
   206	height = Inches(2)
   207	
   208	table = slide.shapes.add_table(rows, cols, left, top, width, height).table
   209	
   210	# Set column widths
   211	table.columns[0].width = Inches(2)
   212	table.columns[1].width = Inches(3)
   213	table.columns[2].width = Inches(3)
   214	
   215	# Add headers
   216	headers = ['Product', 'Q3 Sales', 'Q4 Sales']
   217	for i, header in enumerate(headers):
   218	    cell = table.cell(0, i)
   219	    cell.text = header
   220	    cell.text_frame.paragraphs[0].font.bold = True
   221	
   222	# Add data
   223	data = [
   224	    ['Widget A', '$10,000', '$12,500'],
   225	    ['Widget B', '$8,000', '$9,200'],
   226	    ['Widget C', '$15,000', '$18,000'],
   227	]
   228	for row_idx, row_data in enumerate(data, 1):
   229	    for col_idx, value in enumerate(row_data):
   230	        table.cell(row_idx, col_idx).text = value
   231	```
   232	
   233	### Charts
   234	```python
   235	from pptx.chart.data import CategoryChartData
   236	from pptx.enum.chart import XL_CHART_TYPE
   237	
   238	# Chart data
   239	chart_data = CategoryChartData()
   240	chart_data.categories = ['Q1', 'Q2', 'Q3', 'Q4']
   241	chart_data.add_series('Sales', (19.2, 21.4, 16.7, 23.8))
   242	chart_data.add_series('Expenses', (12.1, 15.3, 14.2, 18.1))
   243	
   244	# Add chart
   245	x, y, cx, cy = Inches(1), Inches(2), Inches(8), Inches(4)
   246	chart = slide.shapes.add_chart(
   247	    XL_CHART_TYPE.COLUMN_CLUSTERED,
   248	    x, y, cx, cy, chart_data
   249	).chart
   250	
   251	# Customize
   252	chart.has_legend = True
   253	chart.legend.include_in_layout = False
   254	```

   256	### Formatting
   257	
   258	#### Text Formatting
   259	```python
   260	from pptx.dml.color import RGBColor
   261	
   262	run = p.runs[0]
   263	run.font.name = 'Arial'
   264	run.font.size = Pt(24)
   265	run.font.bold = True
   266	run.font.italic = True
   267	run.font.color.rgb = RGBColor(0x00, 0x66, 0xCC)
   268	```
   269	
   270	#### Shape Fill & Line
   271	```python
   272	from pptx.dml.color import RGBColor
   273	
   274	shape.fill.solid()
   275	shape.fill.fore_color.rgb = RGBColor(0x00, 0x80, 0x00)
   276	
   277	shape.line.color.rgb = RGBColor(0x00, 0x00, 0x00)
   278	shape.line.width = Pt(2)
   279	```
   280	
   281	#### Paragraph Alignment
   282	```python
   283	from pptx.enum.text import PP_ALIGN
   284	
   285	p.alignment = PP_ALIGN.CENTER  # LEFT, RIGHT, JUSTIFY
   286	```
   287	
   288	## Best Practices
   289	
   290	1. **Use Templates**: Start with a .pptx template for consistent branding
   291	2. **Layout First**: Plan slide structure before coding
   292	3. **Reuse Slide Masters**: Maintain consistency across presentations
   293	4. **Optimize Images**: Compress images before adding
   294	5. **Test Output**: Always verify generated presentations
   295	
   296	## Common Patterns
   297	
   298	### Slide Deck Generator
   299	```python
   300	def create_deck(title, slides_content):
   301	    prs = Presentation()
   302	    
   303	    # Title slide
   304	    slide = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[0])
   305	    slide.shapes.title.text = title
   306	    
   307	    # Content slides
   308	    for slide_data in slides_content:
   309	        slide = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[1])
   310	        slide.shapes.title.text = slide_data['title']
   311	        
   312	        body = slide.placeholders[1]
   313	        tf = body.text_frame
   314	        for i, point in enumerate(slide_data['points']):
   315	            if i == 0:
   316	                tf.text = point
   317	            else:
   318	                p = tf.add_paragraph()
   319	                p.text = point
   320	    
   321	    return prs
   322	```
   323	
   324	### Data-Driven Charts
   325	```python
   326	def add_bar_chart(slide, title, categories, values):
   327	    from pptx.chart.data import CategoryChartData
   328	    from pptx.enum.chart import XL_CHART_TYPE
   329	    
   330	    chart_data = CategoryChartData()
   331	    chart_data.categories = categories
   332	    chart_data.add_series('Values', values)
   333	    
   334	    chart = slide.shapes.add_chart(
   335	        XL_CHART_TYPE.BAR_CLUSTERED,
   336	        Inches(1), Inches(2),
   337	        Inches(8), Inches(4),
   338	        chart_data
   339	    ).chart
   340	    
   341	    chart.chart_title.text_frame.text = title
   342	    return chart
   343	```
   344	
   345	## Examples
   346	
   347	### Example 1: Create a Pitch Deck
   348	```python
   349	from pptx import Presentation
   350	from pptx.util import Inches, Pt
   351	
   352	prs = Presentation()
   353	
   354	# Slide 1: Title
   355	slide = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[0])
   356	slide.shapes.title.text = "StartupX"
   357	slide.placeholders[1].text = "Revolutionizing Document Processing"
   358	
   359	# Slide 2: Problem
   360	slide = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[1])
   361	slide.shapes.title.text = "The Problem"
   362	body = slide.placeholders[1].text_frame
   363	body.text = "Manual document processing costs businesses $1T annually"
   364	p = body.add_paragraph()
   365	p.text = "Average worker spends 20% of time on document tasks"
   366	p.level = 1
   367	
   368	# Slide 3: Solution
   369	slide = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[1])
   370	slide.shapes.title.text = "Our Solution"
   371	body = slide.placeholders[1].text_frame
   372	body.text = "AI-powered document automation"
   373	body.add_paragraph().text = "90% faster processing"
   374	body.add_paragraph().text = "99.5% accuracy"
   375	body.add_paragraph().text = "Works with existing tools"
   376	
   377	# Slide 4: Market
   378	slide = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[5])  # Title only
   379	slide.shapes.title.text = "Market Opportunity: $50B by 2028"
   380	
   381	# Add chart
   382	from pptx.chart.data import CategoryChartData
   383	from pptx.enum.chart import XL_CHART_TYPE
   384	
   385	data = CategoryChartData()
   386	data.categories = ['2024', '2025', '2026', '2027', '2028']
   387	data.add_series('Market Size ($B)', [30, 35, 40, 45, 50])
   388	
   389	slide.shapes.add_chart(
   390	    XL_CHART_TYPE.LINE,
   391	    Inches(1), Inches(1.5),
   392	    Inches(8), Inches(5),
   393	    data
   394	)
   395	
   396	prs.save('pitch_deck.pptx')
   397	```
   398	
   399	### Example 2: Report with Data Table
   400	```python
   401	from pptx import Presentation
   402	from pptx.util import Inches, Pt
   403	
   404	prs = Presentation()
   405	
   406	# Title slide
   407	slide = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[0])
   408	slide.shapes.title.text = "Sales Performance Report"
   409	slide.placeholders[1].text = "Q4 2024"
   410	
   411	# Data slide
   412	slide = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[5])
   413	slide.shapes.title.text = "Regional Performance"
   414	
   415	# Create table
   416	table = slide.shapes.add_table(5, 4, Inches(0.5), Inches(1.5), Inches(9), Inches(4)).table
   417	
   418	# Headers
   419	headers = ['Region', 'Revenue', 'Growth', 'Target']
   420	for i, h in enumerate(headers):
   421	    table.cell(0, i).text = h
   422	    table.cell(0, i).text_frame.paragraphs[0].font.bold = True
   423	
   424	# Data
   425	data = [
   426	    ['North America', '$5.2M', '+15%', 'Met'],
   427	    ['Europe', '$3.8M', '+12%', 'Met'],
   428	    ['Asia Pacific', '$2.9M', '+28%', 'Exceeded'],
   429	    ['Latin America', '$1.1M', '+8%', 'Below'],
   430	]
   431	for row_idx, row_data in enumerate(data, 1):
   432	    for col_idx, value in enumerate(row_data):
   433	        table.cell(row_idx, col_idx).text = value
   434	
   435	prs.save('sales_report.pptx')
   436	```

   438	## Limitations
   439	
   440	- Cannot render complex animations
   441	- Limited SmartArt support
   442	- No video embedding via API
   443	- Master slide editing is complex
   444	- Chart types limited to standard Office charts

1	# Global Renewable Energy in 2025: How Far Have We Come?
     2	
     3	## Source
     4	
     5	Our World in Data – Renewable Energy  
     6	URL: https://ourworldindata.org/renewable-energy  
     7	Authors: Hannah Ritchie, Max Roser, Pablo Rosado  
     8	Data sources: Ember (2026); Energy Institute – Statistical Review of World Energy (2025)
     9	
    10	## The Urgency: Why Renewables Matter
    11	
    12	Since the Industrial Revolution, most countries' energy systems have become dominated by fossil fuels. Three-quarters of global greenhouse gas emissions come from burning fossil fuels for energy. Fossil fuel combustion is also responsible for local air pollution that causes at least 5 million premature deaths per year. To reduce CO₂ emissions and air pollution, the world must rapidly shift toward low-carbon energy sources — nuclear and renewable technologies.
    13	
    14	Renewable energy includes solar, wind, hydropower, geothermal, bioenergy, wave, and tidal sources. Traditional biomass (important in lower-income settings) is typically excluded from modern renewable statistics.
    15	
    16	## Renewables in the Primary Energy Mix
    17	
    18	Approximately one-seventh (~14%) of the world's primary energy now comes from renewable technologies (2024 data, substitution method). Primary energy encompasses electricity, transport, and heating combined. Because transport and heating are harder to decarbonize (more reliant on oil and gas), the renewable share in the total energy mix is lower than in the electricity mix alone.
    19	
    20	![Share of primary energy from renewables by country, 2024](./assets/figure_2.jpg)
    21	
    22	Regional variation is significant. Countries like Norway, Brazil, and New Zealand derive large shares of primary energy from renewables, while fossil-fuel-producing nations in the Middle East and parts of Asia remain below 5%.
    23	
    24	## Renewables in the Electricity Mix
    25	
    26	Globally, almost one-third of electricity now comes from renewable sources (2025). This is substantially higher than the primary energy share because electricity is the sector where renewables have made the most progress.
    27	
    28	![Share of electricity from renewables by country, 2025](./assets/figure_1.jpg)
    29	
    30	| Region / Country | Renewable Share of Electricity (approx.) |
    31	|---|---|
    32	| Norway | ~98% |
    33	| Brazil | ~85% |
    34	| Canada | ~65% |
    35	| Germany | ~55% |
    36	| China | ~35% |
    37	| United States | ~25% |
    38	| India | ~25% |
    39	| World average | ~30% |
    40	| Saudi Arabia | <2% |
    41	| South Africa | ~10% |
    42	
    43	Several African and Middle Eastern countries have renewable electricity shares below 10%, reflecting both fossil fuel dependence and limited investment in renewables.
    44	
    45	## Breakdown by Technology: Hydro, Wind, and Solar
    46	
    47	**Hydropower** remains the single largest renewable electricity source, accounting for roughly half of all renewable generation. It has been generating electricity at scale for over a century. Top producers include China, Brazil, and Canada.
    48	
    49	![Hydropower generation by country, 2025](./assets/figure_6.jpg)
    50	
    51	**Wind energy** has grown rapidly and is now a major contributor, especially in Europe, China, and the United States. Wind generation includes both onshore and offshore installations.
    52	
    53	![Wind power generation by country, 2025](./assets/figure_8.jpg)
    54	
    55	**Solar energy** is the fastest-growing source. Global solar generation has increased dramatically since 2010, driven by falling costs and policy support.
    56	
    57	| Technology | Approx. Global Generation (2024, TWh) | Share of Renewable Electricity |
    58	|---|---|---|
    59	| Hydropower | ~4,500 | ~47% |
    60	| Wind | ~2,400 | ~25% |
    61	| Solar | ~2,000 | ~21% |
    62	| Other renewables (geothermal, biomass, wave, tidal) | ~700 | ~7% |
    63	
    64	While hydropower still leads, wind and solar combined now nearly match hydro's output and are growing much faster.
    65	
    66	## Access and Regional Disparities
    67	
    68	The transition to renewables is highly uneven. Scandinavian countries, Brazil, and Canada benefit from abundant hydropower. European nations like Denmark and Germany have invested heavily in wind and solar. Meanwhile, much of Sub-Saharan Africa has minimal renewable electricity infrastructure, and many Middle Eastern nations remain almost entirely dependent on fossil fuels for electricity.
    69	
    70	![Share of electricity from hydropower by country, 2025](./assets/figure_3.jpg)
    71	
    72	## Key Findings
    73	
    74	- **~14% of global primary energy** and **~30% of global electricity** now come from renewable sources — a significant milestone but far from sufficient for climate targets.
    75	- **Hydropower remains dominant**, generating roughly half of all renewable electricity, but its growth potential is limited compared to wind and solar.
    76	- **Wind and solar are the fastest-growing energy technologies** in history; combined, they now produce nearly as much electricity as hydropower.
    77	- **Stark regional disparities persist**: Scandinavia and Latin America exceed 60–90% renewable electricity, while much of the Middle East and Sub-Saharan Africa remain below 10%.
    78	- **Transport and heating lag far behind electricity** in the renewable transition, keeping the overall primary energy share much lower than the electricity share.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Generate a 9-slide 16:9 PowerPoint presentation on Global Renewable Energy in 2025.
Follows the pptx-manipulation skill and the task_input.json structural requirements.
"""

from pptx import Presentation
from pptx.util import Inches, Pt, Emu
from pptx.enum.text import PP_ALIGN, MSO_ANCHOR
from pptx.enum.shapes import MSO_SHAPE
from pptx.chart.data import CategoryChartData
from pptx.enum.chart import XL_CHART_TYPE
from pptx.dml.color import RGBColor

# ── Constants ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
SLIDE_WIDTH = Inches(13.333)
SLIDE_HEIGHT = Inches(7.5)

# Color palette: analytical, accessible, data-forward
COLOR_DARK = RGBColor(0x1A, 0x1A, 0x2E)       # near-black for titles
COLOR_MID = RGBColor(0x33, 0x33, 0x4D)        # dark slate for subtitles
COLOR_BODY = RGBColor(0x44, 0x44, 0x44)       # body text
COLOR_ACCENT = RGBColor(0x00, 0x7A, 0x6E)     # teal accent
COLOR_ACCENT2 = RGBColor(0x2E, 0x7D, 0x32)    # green accent
COLOR_ACCENT3 = RGBColor(0xF5, 0x7C, 0x00)    # amber accent
COLOR_WHITE = RGBColor(0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF)
COLOR_LIGHT_BG = RGBColor(0xF5, 0xF7, 0xFA)

ASSETS_DIR = "/app/benchmark/assets"
OUTPUT_PATH = "/app/output/final_deck.pptx"

# ── Helpers ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def set_slide_size(prs):
    prs.slide_width = SLIDE_WIDTH
    prs.slide_height = SLIDE_HEIGHT


def add_text_box(slide, left, top, width, height, text, font_size=Pt(14),
                 bold=False, color=COLOR_BODY, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT,
                 font_name="Calibri", italic=False):
    tf = slide.shapes.add_textbox(left, top, width, height).text_frame
    tf.word_wrap = True
    p = tf.paragraphs[0]
    p.text = text
    p.font.size = font_size
    p.font.bold = bold
    p.font.italic = italic
    p.font.color.rgb = color
    p.font.name = font_name
    p.alignment = align
    return tf


def add_bullet_text(slide, left, top, width, height, bullets,
                    font_size=Pt(16), color=COLOR_BODY, font_name="Calibri",
                    bullet_color=COLOR_ACCENT):
    tf = slide.shapes.add_textbox(left, top, width, height).text_frame
    tf.word_wrap = True
    for i, txt in enumerate(bullets):
        if i == 0:
            p = tf.paragraphs[0]
        else:
            p = tf.add_paragraph()
        p.text = txt
        p.font.size = font_size
        p.font.color.rgb = color
        p.font.name = font_name
        p.space_after = Pt(10)
        p.level = 0
    return tf


def add_table(slide, left, top, width, height, headers, rows,
              header_fill=COLOR_ACCENT, header_text=COLOR_WHITE,
              font_size=Pt(12)):
    table = slide.shapes.add_table(1 + len(rows), len(headers),
                                   left, top, width, height).table
    # header
    for i, h in enumerate(headers):
        cell = table.cell(0, i)
        cell.text = h
        p = cell.text_frame.paragraphs[0]
        p.font.bold = True
        p.font.size = font_size
        p.font.color.rgb = header_text
        p.font.name = "Calibri"
        p.alignment = PP_ALIGN.CENTER
        cell.fill.solid()
        cell.fill.fore_color.rgb = header_fill
    # rows
    for r_idx, row in enumerate(rows, 1):
        for c_idx, val in enumerate(row):
            cell = table.cell(r_idx, c_idx)
            cell.text = str(val)
            p = cell.text_frame.paragraphs[0]
            p.font.size = font_size
            p.font.color.rgb = COLOR_BODY
            p.font.name = "Calibri"
            p.alignment = PP_ALIGN.CENTER
            if r_idx % 2 == 0:
                cell.fill.solid()
                cell.fill.fore_color.rgb = COLOR_LIGHT_BG
    return table


def add_footer(slide, text="Source: Our World in Data – Renewable Energy"):
    add_text_box(slide, Inches(0.4), Inches(7.1), Inches(8), Inches(0.3),
                 text, font_size=Pt(10), color=RGBColor(0x88, 0x88, 0x88),
                 italic=True)


def add_slide_number(slide, num, total=9):
    add_text_box(slide, Inches(12.0), Inches(7.1), Inches(1.0), Inches(0.3),
                 f"{num}/{total}", font_size=Pt(10),
                 color=RGBColor(0x88, 0x88, 0x88), align=PP_ALIGN.RIGHT)


# ── Slide Builders ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def build_title_slide(prs):
    slide_layout = prs.slide_layouts[6]  # blank
    slide = prs.slides.add_slide(slide_layout)

    # subtle top accent bar
    bar = slide.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.RECTANGLE, 0, 0, SLIDE_WIDTH, Inches(0.15))
    bar.fill.solid()
    bar.fill.fore_color.rgb = COLOR_ACCENT
    bar.line.fill.background()

    # title
    title_tf = slide.shapes.add_textbox(Inches(0.8), Inches(2.2), Inches(11.7), Inches(1.5)).text_frame
    title_tf.word_wrap = True
    p = title_tf.paragraphs[0]
    p.text = "Global Renewable Energy in 2025: How Far Have We Come?"
    p.font.size = Pt(44)
    p.font.bold = True
    p.font.color.rgb = COLOR_DARK
    p.font.name = "Calibri Light"
    p.alignment = PP_ALIGN.LEFT

    # subtitle
    sub_tf = slide.shapes.add_textbox(Inches(0.8), Inches(3.8), Inches(11.7), Inches(1.0)).text_frame
    sub_tf.word_wrap = True
    p = sub_tf.paragraphs[0]
    p.text = "A data-driven overview of renewable energy trends across primary energy and electricity generation"
    p.font.size = Pt(20)
    p.font.color.rgb = COLOR_MID
    p.font.name = "Calibri"
    p.alignment = PP_ALIGN.LEFT

    # source line
    src_tf = slide.shapes.add_textbox(Inches(0.8), Inches(5.0), Inches(11.7), Inches(0.6)).text_frame
    p = src_tf.paragraphs[0]
    p.text = "Source: Our World in Data – Renewable Energy  |  Authors: Hannah Ritchie, Max Roser, Pablo Rosado"
    p.font.size = Pt(12)
    p.font.color.rgb = RGBColor(0x66, 0x66, 0x66)
    p.font.italic = True
    p.font.name = "Calibri"

    add_footer(slide)
    add_slide_number(slide, 1)
    return slide


def build_fossil_fuel_slide(prs):
    slide_layout = prs.slide_layouts[6]
    slide = prs.slides.add_slide(slide_layout)

    # title
    add_text_box(slide, Inches(0.5), Inches(0.4), Inches(12.3), Inches(0.9),
                 "75% of Global GHG Emissions Still Come from Fossil Fuels",
                 font_size=Pt(32), bold=True, color=COLOR_DARK)

    # accent bar under title
    bar = slide.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.RECTANGLE, Inches(0.5), Inches(1.2), Inches(2.5), Inches(0.06))
    bar.fill.solid()
    bar.fill.fore_color.rgb = COLOR_ACCENT3
    bar.line.fill.background()

    # left column: key stats
    stats = [
        "• Three-quarters of global greenhouse gas emissions come from burning fossil fuels for energy.",
        "• Fossil fuel combustion causes at least 5 million premature deaths per year from local air pollution.",
        "• Since the Industrial Revolution, most countries' energy systems have become dominated by coal, oil, and gas.",
        "• To reduce CO₂ emissions and air pollution, the world must rapidly shift toward low-carbon sources — nuclear and renewable technologies."
    ]
    tf = slide.shapes.add_textbox(Inches(0.5), Inches(1.6), Inches(5.8), Inches(5.0)).text_frame
    tf.word_wrap = True
    for i, txt in enumerate(stats):
        if i == 0:
            p = tf.paragraphs[0]
        else:
            p = tf.add_paragraph()
        p.text = txt
        p.font.size = Pt(18)
        p.font.color.rgb = COLOR_BODY
        p.font.name = "Calibri"
        p.space_after = Pt(16)
        p.level = 0

    # right column: callout box
    box = slide.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.ROUNDED_RECTANGLE,
                                 Inches(6.6), Inches(1.8), Inches(6.0), Inches(3.8))
    box.fill.solid()
    box.fill.fore_color.rgb = RGBColor(0xFF, 0xF3, 0xE0)
    box.line.color.rgb = COLOR_ACCENT3
    box.line.width = Pt(2)

    box_tf = box.text_frame
    box_tf.word_wrap = True
    p = box_tf.paragraphs[0]
    p.text = "The Urgency"
    p.font.size = Pt(24)
    p.font.bold = True
    p.font.color.rgb = COLOR_ACCENT3
    p.font.name = "Calibri"
    p.alignment = PP_ALIGN.CENTER

    p2 = box_tf.add_paragraph()
    p2.text = "\nRenewable energy includes solar, wind, hydropower, geothermal, bioenergy, wave, and tidal sources. Traditional biomass is typically excluded from modern renewable statistics."
    p2.font.size = Pt(16)
    p2.font.color.rgb = COLOR_BODY
    p2.font.name = "Calibri"
    p2.alignment = PP_ALIGN.CENTER

    add_footer(slide)
    add_slide_number(slide, 2)
    return slide


def build_primary_energy_slide(prs):
    slide_layout = prs.slide_layouts[6]
    slide = prs.slides.add_slide(slide_layout)

    add_text_box(slide, Inches(0.5), Inches(0.4), Inches(12.3), Inches(0.9),
                 "Renewables Now Supply ~14% of Global Primary Energy",
                 font_size=Pt(32), bold=True, color=COLOR_DARK)

    bar = slide.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.RECTANGLE, Inches(0.5), Inches(1.2), Inches(2.5), Inches(0.06))
    bar.fill.solid()
    bar.fill.fore_color.rgb = COLOR_ACCENT
    bar.line.fill.background()

    # left text
    tf = slide.shapes.add_textbox(Inches(0.5), Inches(1.5), Inches(5.5), Inches(5.0)).text_frame
    tf.word_wrap = True
    bullets = [
        "Approximately one-seventh (~14%) of the world's primary energy now comes from renewable technologies (2024 data, substitution method).",
        "Primary energy encompasses electricity, transport, and heating combined.",
        "Because transport and heating are harder to decarbonise (more reliant on oil and gas), the renewable share in total energy is lower than in electricity alone.",
        "Regional variation is significant: Norway, Brazil, and New Zealand derive large shares from renewables, while fossil-fuel-producing nations in the Middle East and parts of Asia remain below 5%."
    ]
    for i, txt in enumerate(bullets):
        if i == 0:
            p = tf.paragraphs[0]
        else:
            p = tf.add_paragraph()
        p.text = txt
        p.font.size = Pt(16)
        p.font.color.rgb = COLOR_BODY
        p.font.name = "Calibri"
        p.space_after = Pt(12)

    # right image
    slide.shapes.add_picture(f"{ASSETS_DIR}/figure_2.jpg",
                             Inches(6.4), Inches(1.4),
                             width=Inches(6.6))

    add_footer(slide, "Source: Our World in Data – Renewable Energy  |  Map: Share of primary energy from renewables by country, 2024")
    add_slide_number(slide, 3)
    return slide


def build_generation_growth_slide(prs):
    slide_layout = prs.slide_layouts[6]
    slide = prs.slides.add_slide(slide_layout)

    add_text_box(slide, Inches(0.5), Inches(0.35), Inches(12.3), Inches(0.9),
                 "Renewable Electricity Generation Is Growing Rapidly, Led by Wind and Solar",
                 font_size=Pt(30), bold=True, color=COLOR_DARK)

    bar = slide.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.RECTANGLE, Inches(0.5), Inches(1.15), Inches(2.5), Inches(0.06))
    bar.fill.solid()
    bar.fill.fore_color.rgb = COLOR_ACCENT2
    bar.line.fill.background()

    # chart data
    chart_data = CategoryChartData()
    chart_data.categories = ['Hydropower', 'Wind', 'Solar', 'Other renewables']
    chart_data.add_series('Generation (TWh)', (4500, 2400, 2000, 700))

    chart = slide.shapes.add_chart(
        XL_CHART_TYPE.COLUMN_CLUSTERED,
        Inches(0.5), Inches(1.5), Inches(7.0), Inches(5.0),
        chart_data
    ).chart

    chart.has_legend = False
    chart.chart_title.text_frame.text = "Global Renewable Electricity Generation by Technology (2024, TWh)"
    chart.chart_title.text_frame.paragraphs[0].font.size = Pt(14)
    chart.chart_title.text_frame.paragraphs[0].font.color.rgb = COLOR_MID

    # colour the series
    from pptx.enum.chart import XL_LEGEND_POSITION
    plot = chart.plots[0]
    plot.series[0].format.fill.solid()
    plot.series[0].format.fill.fore_color.rgb = RGBColor(0x42, 0x7A, 0xC4)  # hydro blue

    # right side: key insights
    insights = [
        "Key Insights",
        "",
        "• Hydropower remains the single largest source at ~4,500 TWh (~47% of renewable electricity).",
        "• Wind has grown rapidly to ~2,400 TWh (~25%).",
        "• Solar is the fastest-growing source at ~2,000 TWh (~21%), with dramatic growth since 2010 driven by falling costs and policy support.",
        "• Other renewables (geothermal, biomass, wave, tidal) contribute ~700 TWh (~7%).",
        "",
        "Wind and solar combined now nearly match hydropower's output and are growing much faster."
    ]
    tf = slide.shapes.add_textbox(Inches(7.8), Inches(1.6), Inches(5.0), Inches(5.0)).text_frame
    tf.word_wrap = True
    for i, txt in enumerate(insights):
        if i == 0:
            p = tf.paragraphs[0]
            p.font.bold = True
            p.font.size = Pt(18)
            p.font.color.rgb = COLOR_ACCENT
        else:
            p = tf.add_paragraph()
            p.text = txt
            p.font.size = Pt(15) if txt.startswith("•") else Pt(14)
            p.font.color.rgb = COLOR_BODY
            p.font.italic = (txt == "Wind and solar combined now nearly match hydropower's output and are growing much faster.")
            p.space_after = Pt(8)
        p.font.name = "Calibri"

    add_footer(slide)
    add_slide_number(slide, 4)
    return slide


def build_electricity_mix_slide(prs):
    slide_layout = prs.slide_layouts[6]
    slide = prs.slides.add_slide(slide_layout)

    add_text_box(slide, Inches(0.5), Inches(0.35), Inches(12.3), Inches(0.9),
                 "Almost One-Third of Global Electricity Now Comes from Renewables",
                 font_size=Pt(30), bold=True, color=COLOR_DARK)

    bar = slide.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.RECTANGLE, Inches(0.5), Inches(1.15), Inches(2.5), Inches(0.06))
    bar.fill.solid()
    bar.fill.fore_color.rgb = COLOR_ACCENT
    bar.line.fill.background()

    # map image
    slide.shapes.add_picture(f"{ASSETS_DIR}/figure_1.jpg",
                             Inches(0.4), Inches(1.4),
                             width=Inches(7.8))

    # data table
    headers = ["Country / Region", "Renewable Share"]
    rows = [
        ["Norway", "~98%"],
        ["Brazil", "~85%"],
        ["Canada", "~65%"],
        ["China", "~35%"],
        ["United States", "~25%"],
        ["India", "~25%"],
        ["Saudi Arabia", "<2%"],
    ]
    table = add_table(slide, Inches(8.5), Inches(1.6), Inches(4.2), Inches(3.8),
                      headers, rows, header_fill=COLOR_ACCENT,
                      header_text=COLOR_WHITE, font_size=Pt(13))

    # caption under table
    add_text_box(slide, Inches(8.5), Inches(5.5), Inches(4.2), Inches(0.8),
                 "World average: ~30%\nSeveral African and Middle Eastern countries remain below 10%.",
                 font_size=Pt(13), color=COLOR_BODY, italic=True)

    add_footer(slide, "Source: Our World in Data – Renewable Energy  |  Map: Share of electricity from renewables by country, 2025")
    add_slide_number(slide, 5)
    return slide


def build_hydropower_slide(prs):
    slide_layout = prs.slide_layouts[6]
    slide = prs.slides.add_slide(slide_layout)

    add_text_box(slide, Inches(0.5), Inches(0.4), Inches(12.3), Inches(0.9),
                 "Hydropower Remains the Largest Renewable Source at ~50% of Generation",
                 font_size=Pt(30), bold=True, color=COLOR_DARK)

    bar = slide.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.RECTANGLE, Inches(0.5), Inches(1.2), Inches(2.5), Inches(0.06))
    bar.fill.solid()
    bar.fill.fore_color.rgb = RGBColor(0x42, 0x7A, 0xC4)
    bar.line.fill.background()

    # left text
    bullets = [
        "Hydropower accounts for roughly half of all renewable electricity generation (~4,500 TWh in 2024).",
        "It has been generating electricity at scale for over a century.",
        "Top producers include China, Brazil, and Canada.",
        "While hydropower still leads, its growth potential is limited compared to wind and solar."
    ]
    tf = slide.shapes.add_textbox(Inches(0.5), Inches(1.6), Inches(5.5), Inches(4.5)).text_frame
    tf.word_wrap = True
    for i, txt in enumerate(bullets):
        if i == 0:
            p = tf.paragraphs[0]
        else:
            p = tf.add_paragraph()
        p.text = txt
        p.font.size = Pt(17)
        p.font.color.rgb = COLOR_BODY
        p.font.name = "Calibri"
        p.space_after = Pt(14)

    # right image
    slide.shapes.add_picture(f"{ASSETS_DIR}/figure_6.jpg",
                             Inches(6.4), Inches(1.4),
                             width=Inches(6.6))

    add_footer(slide, "Source: Our World in Data – Renewable Energy  |  Map: Hydropower generation by country, 2025")
    add_slide_number(slide, 6)
    return slide


def build_wind_solar_slide(prs):
    slide_layout = prs.slide_layouts[6]
    slide = prs.slides.add_slide(slide_layout)

    add_text_box(slide, Inches(0.5), Inches(0.35), Inches(12.3), Inches(0.9),
                 "Wind and Solar Are the Fastest-Growing Energy Technologies in History",
                 font_size=Pt(30), bold=True, color=COLOR_DARK)

    bar = slide.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.RECTANGLE, Inches(0.5), Inches(1.15), Inches(2.5), Inches(0.06))
    bar.fill.solid()
    bar.fill.fore_color.rgb = COLOR_ACCENT2
    bar.line.fill.background()

    # left image
    slide.shapes.add_picture(f"{ASSETS_DIR}/figure_8.jpg",
                             Inches(0.4), Inches(1.4),
                             width=Inches(6.4))

    # right comparison box
    box = slide.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.ROUNDED_RECTANGLE,
                                 Inches(7.0), Inches(1.5), Inches(6.0), Inches(4.8))
    box.fill.solid()
    box.fill.fore_color.rgb = RGBColor(0xE8, 0xF5, 0xE9)
    box.line.color.rgb = COLOR_ACCENT2
    box.line.width = Pt(2)

    box_tf = box.text_frame
    box_tf.word_wrap = True

    p = box_tf.paragraphs[0]
    p.text = "Wind vs. Solar Comparison (2024)"
    p.font.size = Pt(20)
    p.font.bold = True
    p.font.color.rgb = COLOR_ACCENT2
    p.font.name = "Calibri"
    p.alignment = PP_ALIGN.LEFT

    lines = [
        "",
        "Wind Energy",
        "  • Generation: ~2,400 TWh",
        "  • Share of renewable electricity: ~25%",
        "  • Major markets: Europe, China, United States",
        "  • Includes onshore and offshore installations",
        "",
        "Solar Energy",
        "  • Generation: ~2,000 TWh",
        "  • Share of renewable electricity: ~21%",
        "  • Fastest-growing source with dramatic growth since 2010",
        "  • Driven by falling costs and policy support",
        "",
        "Combined, wind + solar (~4,400 TWh) now nearly match hydropower (~4,500 TWh)."
    ]
    for txt in lines:
        p = box_tf.add_paragraph()
        p.text = txt
        if txt in ("Wind Energy", "Solar Energy"):
            p.font.bold = True
            p.font.size = Pt(16)
            p.font.color.rgb = COLOR_DARK
        elif txt.startswith("Combined,"):
            p.font.italic = True
            p.font.size = Pt(14)
            p.font.color.rgb = COLOR_MID
        else:
            p.font.size = Pt(14)
            p.font.color.rgb = COLOR_BODY
        p.font.name = "Calibri"
        p.space_after = Pt(4)

    add_footer(slide, "Source: Our World in Data – Renewable Energy  |  Map: Wind power generation by country, 2025")
    add_slide_number(slide, 7)
    return slide


def build_regional_slide(prs):
    slide_layout = prs.slide_layouts[6]
    slide = prs.slides.add_slide(slide_layout)

    add_text_box(slide, Inches(0.5), Inches(0.35), Inches(12.3), Inches(0.9),
                 "Stark Regional Gaps: Sub-Saharan Africa Lags While Scandinavia and Latin America Lead",
                 font_size=Pt(28), bold=True, color=COLOR_DARK)

    bar = slide.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.RECTANGLE, Inches(0.5), Inches(1.1), Inches(2.5), Inches(0.06))
    bar.fill.solid()
    bar.fill.fore_color.rgb = COLOR_ACCENT3
    bar.line.fill.background()

    # left image
    slide.shapes.add_picture(f"{ASSETS_DIR}/figure_3.jpg",
                             Inches(0.4), Inches(1.4),
                             width=Inches(6.4))

    # right text
    bullets = [
        "The transition to renewables is highly uneven across regions.",
        "",
        "Leaders:",
        "  • Scandinavia, Brazil, and Canada benefit from abundant hydropower (65–98% renewable electricity).",
        "  • European nations like Denmark and Germany have invested heavily in wind and solar.",
        "",
        "Laggards:",
        "  • Much of Sub-Saharan Africa has minimal renewable electricity infrastructure.",
        "  • Many Middle Eastern nations remain almost entirely dependent on fossil fuels for electricity (shares below 10%).",
        "",
        "These disparities reflect differences in natural resources, investment capacity, and policy priorities."
    ]
    tf = slide.shapes.add_textbox(Inches(7.0), Inches(1.5), Inches(6.0), Inches(5.2)).text_frame
    tf.word_wrap = True
    for i, txt in enumerate(bullets):
        if i == 0:
            p = tf.paragraphs[0]
        else:
            p = tf.add_paragraph()
        p.text = txt
        if txt in ("Leaders:", "Laggards:"):
            p.font.bold = True
            p.font.size = Pt(17)
            p.font.color.rgb = COLOR_ACCENT
        elif txt == "":
            p.font.size = Pt(6)
        else:
            p.font.size = Pt(15)
            p.font.color.rgb = COLOR_BODY
        p.font.name = "Calibri"
        p.space_after = Pt(6)

    add_footer(slide, "Source: Our World in Data – Renewable Energy  |  Map: Share of electricity from hydropower by country, 2025")
    add_slide_number(slide, 8)
    return slide


def build_takeaways_slide(prs):
    slide_layout = prs.slide_layouts[6]
    slide = prs.slides.add_slide(slide_layout)

    add_text_box(slide, Inches(0.5), Inches(0.35), Inches(12.3), Inches(0.9),
                 "Key Takeaways: Renewables Are Growing Fast but the Transition Must Accelerate",
                 font_size=Pt(30), bold=True, color=COLOR_DARK)

    bar = slide.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.RECTANGLE, Inches(0.5), Inches(1.15), Inches(2.5), Inches(0.06))
    bar.fill.solid()
    bar.fill.fore_color.rgb = COLOR_ACCENT
    bar.line.fill.background()

    # 5 takeaway boxes in a 2x3-ish grid
    takeaways = [
        ("~14% of primary energy, ~30% of electricity",
         "Renewables have reached significant milestones, but shares remain far below what is needed for climate targets."),
        ("Hydropower still dominates",
         "Generating roughly half of all renewable electricity, yet its growth potential is limited compared to wind and solar."),
        ("Wind and solar are the fastest-growing technologies in history",
         "Combined, they now produce nearly as much electricity as hydropower and are expanding rapidly."),
        ("Stark regional disparities persist",
         "Scandinavia and Latin America exceed 60–98% renewable electricity; much of the Middle East and Sub-Saharan Africa remain below 10%."),
        ("Transport and heating lag far behind electricity",
         "The harder-to-decarbonise sectors keep overall primary energy share much lower than the electricity share."),
    ]

    positions = [
        (Inches(0.5), Inches(1.5)),
        (Inches(4.5), Inches(1.5)),
        (Inches(8.5), Inches(1.5)),
        (Inches(0.5), Inches(4.2)),
        (Inches(4.5), Inches(4.2)),
    ]

    for (left, top), (head, body) in zip(positions, takeaways):
        box = slide.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.ROUNDED_RECTANGLE,
                                     left, top, Inches(3.8), Inches(2.4))
        box.fill.solid()
        box.fill.fore_color.rgb = COLOR_LIGHT_BG
        box.line.color.rgb = COLOR_ACCENT
        box.line.width = Pt(1.5)

        btf = box.text_frame
        btf.word_wrap = True
        p = btf.paragraphs[0]
        p.text = head
        p.font.size = Pt(15)
        p.font.bold = True
        p.font.color.rgb = COLOR_ACCENT
        p.font.name = "Calibri"

        p2 = btf.add_paragraph()
        p2.text = "\n" + body
        p2.font.size = Pt(13)
        p2.font.color.rgb = COLOR_BODY
        p2.font.name = "Calibri"

    # forward-looking statement
    stmt = slide.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.RECTANGLE,
                                  Inches(8.5), Inches(4.2), Inches(4.2), Inches(2.4))
    stmt.fill.solid()
    stmt.fill.fore_color.rgb = COLOR_ACCENT
    stmt.line.fill.background()

    stf = stmt.text_frame
    stf.word_wrap = True
    p = stf.paragraphs[0]
    p.text = "The Path Forward"
    p.font.size = Pt(18)
    p.font.bold = True
    p.font.color.rgb = COLOR_WHITE
    p.font.name = "Calibri"
    p.alignment = PP_ALIGN.CENTER

    p2 = stf.add_paragraph()
    p2.text = "\nTo meet climate targets, the pace of renewable deployment must accelerate dramatically — especially in transport, heating, and regions currently left behind."
    p2.font.size = Pt(14)
    p2.font.color.rgb = COLOR_WHITE
    p2.font.name = "Calibri"
    p2.alignment = PP_ALIGN.CENTER

    add_footer(slide)
    add_slide_number(slide, 9)
    return slide


# ── Main ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def main():
    prs = Presentation()
    set_slide_size(prs)

    build_title_slide(prs)
    build_fossil_fuel_slide(prs)
    build_primary_energy_slide(prs)
    build_generation_growth_slide(prs)
    build_electricity_mix_slide(prs)
    build_hydropower_slide(prs)
    build_wind_solar_slide(prs)
    build_regional_slide(prs)
    build_takeaways_slide(prs)

    prs.save(OUTPUT_PATH)
    print(f"Saved presentation to {OUTPUT_PATH}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
